name: Hoi An
title: Holidays in Hoi An
intro: Lantern-lit streets, basket boats and a beach just down the road. Here's what Hoi An is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 6 to 7 hrs ahead of the UK

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 45 days

facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: February to April is the sweet spot, warm and dry with calm sea. May to August is hot but sunny and good for the beach. October and November are the rainy season, when the old town sometimes floods.

things.name: Ancient Town
things.blurb: Lantern-lit lanes, old merchant houses and the Japanese Covered Bridge. Magical after dark.

things.name: Basket boats
things.blurb: Spin round in a round bamboo boat in the coconut palm waterways.

things.name: An Bang Beach
things.blurb: A sandy beach about 10 minutes away by bike or taxi.

things.name: Lantern-making class
things.blurb: Make your own silk lantern to take home.

things.name: Cycling the rice fields
things.blurb: Flat lanes past paddy fields and water buffalo. Most hotels lend bikes.

things.name: Ba Na Hills
things.blurb: A long cable car to the Golden Bridge held up by giant stone hands.

faqs.question: Is Hoi An good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's small, friendly and easy, with a beach close by and good food everywhere. Traffic is the main hazard, so hold hands when crossing roads.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Seven to ten nights mixes the old town with beach days. Many families combine it with Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City on a two or three week trip.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 45 days without a visa. Your passport must be valid for six months. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: How do you get there?
faqs.answer: Fly to Da Nang, usually with one stop, then it's about 45 minutes by car.
